summary.name: Elicit
summary.one_liner: Elicit is an AI research assistant that searches academic papers and clinical trials, then produces cited reports, systematic review support, and evidence tables.
use_cases: Synthesizing evidence on a research question
Screening and extracting data from papers
Keeping up with new research via routines
summary.what_it_does: Elicit searches over 138 million academic papers and 545,000 clinical trials using semantic search, so exact keywords are not required. It generates customizable research reports based on a process inspired by systematic reviews, where users can change which papers and information are covered. For systematic reviews, it can automate screening and data extraction, and the page claims researchers report up to 80% time savings. It supports sentence-level citations for AI-generated claims and can handle up to 1,000 papers and 20,000 data points at once, presenting results in interactive tables and multi-step workflows. A Library stores sources for reuse across projects.
notable: Semantic search over 138 million academic papers and 545,000 clinical trials
Customizable research reports inspired by systematic reviews
Automated screening and data extraction for systematic reviews
caveats: Systematic review support is described as partial for search and report generation
More data sources are said to be coming soon, implying not all sources are available yet
